evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark and its failure analysis document inconsistent performance, reasoning errors and policy-following failures in tested agents. These earlier results support the concern behind Marcus's assessment, but do not establish the suitability of all relevant systems at publication or test the full capability bundle.

OSWorld reports substantial difficulty with computer tasks, particularly interface grounding and operational knowledge. This is relevant earlier evidence of practical limitations, but interface grounding is narrower than Marcus's grounding in reality and the study does not isolate all the claimed causes.

The GPT-4 evaluation, conducted in January 2024, demonstrates success on defined higher-order theory-of-mind questions. It cautions against interpreting Marcus as claiming an absence of these abilities, but does not demonstrate dependable intention inference within a complete agent.

unresolved_gaps: The retrieved evaluations do not jointly test the full capability bundle in systems representative of the publication-date state.
The studies do not isolate generative AI alone as the cause of the broader suitability limitation.
Success on story-based theory-of-mind questions does not establish dependable interpretation of users' intentions during delegated tasks.
